subject: Tranche synchronization & country SKU alignment for Helio / GlintAI

Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — Helio & GlintAI capacity windows and country SKUs

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week. GlintAI is preparing our 2027 pilot run and we need a clear proposal for dedicated capacity across US / EU / APAC that lines up with our billing tranches. Two asks from procurement and engineering:

1) A country-level SKU matrix (estimated GPU vCPU equivalent per SKU) by region so we can map to our internal chargeback.
2) Recommended tranche windows (activation order + overlap) for a staged ramp: pilot (Q1), scale (Q2–Q3), steady-state (Q4). We need to ensure staged-onboarding doesn't create cross-region contention.

We can share our forecast; attaching the latest demand file (glintai_forecast_Q4_v3.xlsx) for context. Can you get us a first-pass SKU matrix and tranche plan by end of week?

Heads-up — our legal team will likely ask for explicit fallback lanes if a region is constrained.

Best,
Matt
Matt Dunn
Head of Infrastructure, GlintAI

- Deliver a draft SKU matrix (PDF) mapping our common dedicated SKUs to approximate GPU footprint and expected latency bands per region.
- Propose tranche activation windows that avoid simultaneous full-fleet activation in APAC + EU during their respective peak hours; a staggered 7–14 day overlap typically works.
- Provide two fallback options: 1) route to compatible quantized SKU in another region, 2) soft-cap token rate during initial ramp.

Target: draft by Fri 20 Nov EOD PT. Attaching a short template (sku_matrix_proposal_v1.pdf) we will populate. If we need to accelerate, let me know which week in Q1 pilot you prefer to lock.

Matt / Irene — quick technical note on SKU sizing:

- For GlintAI's predicted peak profile (see the forecast): if 70% of requests are <512 tokens we can use our 40-token-batch-optimized SKU (approx 2 x A100-equivalent vGPU per reserved unit) for most steady-state.
- APAC latency sensitivity suggests we reserve a small hot-standby (10–12% of committed) in SG/Tokyo to keep p95 under 120ms.
- For EU we recommend a slightly higher memory SKU for longer-context use cases (chat + retrieval). That SKU costs ~12% more but avoids tail-regression.

Operational suggestion: set two activation windows per tranche — primary (full feature traffic) and a 48-hour shadow ramp where traffic is mirrored at 10–20% to verify KV-cache warm-up and routing.

I can sketch the mapping into the SKU PDF — adding estimates to each line (GPU equiv, p95 latency, recommended cache warm-up).

—Rishi

Adding ops constraints / SLO guardrails:

- If you want p95<120ms in APAC during pilot, plan for a 12% buffer above forecasted committed capacity for the first 30 days. We'll monitor model cache hit rate and token distribution; we'll convert to a permanent buffer or reduce after week 6 based on metrics.
- Canary policy: 3% mirrored traffic, 24h, then 10% for 48h before full switch. Include a rollback window in your runbook (we recommend 6h).
- Log retention note for procurement: cross-region audit logs are retained per the Private offering if you need proofs for compliance.

I'll prepare the short ops checklist to attach to the SKU PDF (will include required runbook steps and monitoring dashboards).

Grace
